headline: Iran executes three men over January protests, accused of working for Israel/US
dek: Iran executed Hassan Divband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh at dawn on Sunday Nov 8 in Karaj (Ghezel Hesar Prison per Hengaw) after the Supreme Court upheld their death sentences. The judiciary says they were convicted of 'participating in operational activities on behalf of the Israeli Zionist…
sources: Iranian judiciary via Mizan Online; Norway-based Iran Human Rights (IHR); Hengaw Organization for Human Rights
fault_line: Were these three foreign agents, as Tehran claims, or protesters hanged on unexamined confessions? The fault line is whether a death sentence for 'working for Israel and America' is evidence or a label.

sections.what_happened: Iran executed Hassan Divband, Hamid Kazemi and Reza Zanganeh at dawn on Sunday Nov 8 in Karaj (Ghezel Hesar Prison per Hengaw) after the Supreme Court upheld their death sentences. The judiciary says they were convicted of 'participating in operational activities on behalf of the Israeli Zionist regime, the United States and hostile groups' during the Jan 8-9 anti-government protests in Karaj -- using firearms, grenades and Molotov cocktails, setting fire to public facilities and damaging an electricity substation. Eight other defendants in the case received 5-10 year prison terms; assets of the three confiscated. Norway-based Iran Human Rights: the hangings bring the number of men hanged over the January protests to at least 39, with many more at risk. Hengaw: the three bring the number of political/religious prisoners executed in Iran in 2026 to 79, including 40 sentenced in connection with the January protests. HRANA reported the death sentences two days earlier (Karaj Revolutionary Court, Branch 2, Judge Sabzevari).
sections.what_verified: Jerusalem Post (T3) + Times of Israel (T3) + The Hindu (T2) + Economic Times + Vanguard + Hengaw all confirm the executions, the names and the judiciary's stated charges, all tracing to Mizan Online. IHR (via Gulf News/AP reporting) and Hengaw independently count the protest-linked running total. Zero mentions in any Nov 8/9 scan (grep) -- genuine miss.
sections.what_disputed: The Israel/US-agent charge is the judiciary's characterisation: the judiciary says confessions, surveillance footage and intelligence reports supported the convictions, but the evidence has not been independently examined and rights groups describe the trials as unfair (JPost). RUNNING-TOTAL DISCREPANCY: IHR counts 'at least 39' hanged over the January protests; Hengaw counts 40 sentenced in connection with the January protests executed in 2026 (and 79 political/religious prisoners executed in 2026 overall). Production must attribute each total to its source, never blend them. An October Iran International investigation counted at least 70 executions in political/security cases Jan 7-Oct 5, incl. 35 connected to the protests -- a different scope again.
sections.why_matters: Three men hanged at dawn in Karaj -- Tehran says they worked for Israel and America during the January protests. The evidence was never independently examined, and rights groups count 39 already hanged over those protests.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP -- Iran executes three men over January protests, accused of working for Israel/US; rights groups count 39-40 protest-linked executions in 2026

totw_analysis: Our read: Three men hanged at dawn in Karaj -- Tehran says they worked for Israel and America during the January protests. The evidence was never independently examined, and rights groups count 39 already hanged over those protests. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Were these three foreign agents, as Tehran claims, or protesters hanged on unexamined confessions? The fault line is whether a death sentence for 'working for Israel and America' is evidence or a label.
